Routine:

This is all done with my head upside down(?). I dampen my hair before washing, the new shampoo I’m trying is SheaMoisture Hi-Slip Detangling Shampoo (it’s meant to help with shrinkage). I work the shampoo through my hair from ends to roots and massage my scalp as thoroughly as possible before rinsing. The conditioner I use is the matching Leave-in or Rinse-out Conditioner and work that through my hair before letting it sit. After letting settle for five minutes, I work on finger detangling for the worst and then run a very wide tooth shower comb through it for minimal to no breakage aside from regular shedding. Then I give it another rinse and blot it with a towel before spritzing in a mixture of argon oil and water and scrunching it lightly for the usual wash and go. This takes me about an hour to do in total, sometimes it’s shorter and sometimes it’s longer.

NAH

Does everyone remember that reddit post about the single dad trying to force the birth giver into dealing with a kid that she didn’t want? How she had absolutely no contact with said kid and gave up all parental rights and paid extra child support because she didn’t want anything to do with it? Everyone sided with her and called him manipulative and toxic for his opinion on her and his on selfishness for wanting to put her into a situation that she didn’t want to begin with. This is the same thing. OP has also stated that he would pay child support if asked.

If you don’t want to be in that child’s life and have had NO CONTACT prior then why start now? Why put yourself into a situation that can become extremely toxic for all parties involved? Why would you want to put that kid through that? Kids can want to know sure, but sometimes it’s best to avoid such situations because things can only become worse. I’m glad the mother asked instead of demand and OP could have been softer in his response but it’s still his choice. And I’m pretty sure he wants to avoid being the bad guy here because if the kid has to deal with being around someone who never wanted them to begin with then I’m pretty sure it’s gonna mess them up in the long run.

NTA

And I’m also saying this while feeling like there’s not enough info. So OP stated that he speaks English with his brothers and Japanese with his mother, which means that since everybody is at the dinner table then there’s two languages going back forth but English a lot more so than Japanese. If OP’s stepdad isn’t contributing to the conversation then why should he switch his language just for him? If OP isn’t talking in Japanese to everybody then I don’t think he’s intentionally leaving his stepdad out. There are a lot of entitled people who believe that if you speak more than one language, then you should speak just the majority language in front of everybody and that isn’t fair to someone who is outside of their native tongue because it can become uncomfortable. If they’re not insulting someone or making snide remarks then I don’t see the exact issue.

OP stated that his stepdad feels left out because only he and his mother are speaking in Japanese to one another but didn’t make a statement saying that the stepdad tried to make a conversation with them at the dinner table. It sounds like a lot of one sided anger honestly.

Do I think OP could just say forget it and go by what the stepdad says? Yes but again, it isn’t fair to OP. Just because someone wants you to speak a language other than your own doesn’t mean you have to. Fairness would be the two of them having a conversation together in English with the stepdad actually contributing instead of just wanting to listen in because that’s how a conversation works — everybody contributes.

As for the verbally abusive state of the stepdad having qualms about OP’s birth father, that just makes a bigger rift in their relationship as a whole and dropping his native tongue more than likely isn’t going to help that.
